name: Executive Order of July 5, 1873 setting apart a joint reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfoot and River Crow (reduced by the Act of April 15, 1874)
citation: Executive Order of July 5, 1873; Act of April 15, 1874, 18 Stat. 28
nations: Amskapi Piikani (Blackfeet Nation; Piegan, Blood and Blackfoot)
Aaniiih (Gros Ventre), Fort Belknap Indian Community
promises: The President set apart a reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfoot and River Crow running from the northwest corner of Dakota south to the Missouri, up the Missouri and the Sun (Medicine) River to the Rocky Mountains, and north to the Canadian line, excepting military reservations (Royce, entry for July 5, 1873).
There was no agreement with the tribes; it was an executive order, and so contained no promise of payment.

breaches.what: Less than a year later Congress redrew the reservation with its southern line on the Marias River and Birch Creek instead of the Sun River; Royce records that a further part was given up by Executive Order of August 19, 1874. Royce shows areas 565 and 574 together as the 1873 reserve.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Act of April 15, 1874, 18 Stat. 28 (boundaries as quoted by the Indian Claims Commission, Docket 279-B findings, 1965); Royce, schedule entry for July 5, 1873

source.title: Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket 279-B, Findings of Fact, August 16, 1965
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.what: The Court of Claims found that 15,289,344 acres (Royce areas 399 and 574) of the land assigned to these tribes by the 1855 treaty were taken under the Act of April 15, 1874 and the Executive Order of August 19, 1874, and that after crediting lands added to their reservation they were deprived of 12,261,749.76 acres without compensation, worth $6,130,874.88 when taken.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Court of Claims, Blackfeet et al. v. United States, No. E-427, 81 Ct. Cl. 101 (April 8, 1935), as recounted by the Indian Claims Commission (1952) and the Court of Claims (1954)

source.title: Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket 279, Opinion of the Commission, December 17, 1952, 2 Ind. Cl. Comm. 302
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.what: The Blackfeet Nation says that after the 1855 treaty more treaties and agreements followed, each taking large parts of its traditional land.

source.title: Blackfeet Nation, Our History (Wayback capture of March 8, 2010)

breaches.quote: More would follow, each taking huge chunks of our traditional land.

compensation: The Court of Claims valued the land taken at $6,130,874.88 and reduced it by offsets to a judgment of $622,465.57; the Court of Claims later recorded that the value, but no interest, was paid in 1935. The Indian Claims Commission (1952) and the Court of Claims (1954) held a later claim for about $18,000,000 in interest barred by that judgment.
today: Royce records the remainder as the reserve of these tribes; it was divided by the agreements ratified on May 1, 1888 into the Blackfeet, Fort Belknap and Fort Peck reservations.

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's own history says that after Lame Bull's Treaty of 1855 more treaties and agreements followed, each taking large parts of its traditional land, made when the people were not equipped to negotiate or even understand them.

openQuestions: The 1935 Court of Claims opinion (81 Ct. Cl. 101) was not opened directly; its findings are taken from the Indian Claims Commission's 1952 account and the 1954 Court of Claims opinion.

The Court of Claims measured the taking from the 1855 treaty lands (Royce 399 and 574), not from the 1873 executive-order boundary; how much of the 1873 reserve south of Birch Creek and the Marias falls in area 399 rather than 574 was not checked on the map.

The statement in 'today' that the rest was divided in 1888 rests on the 1888 agreement's ratifying act (25 Stat. 113), researched in cession-1888-05-01-indians-of-blackfoot-agency; this file did not reopen it.
The Executive Order of July 5, 1873 was read only in Royce's summary, not in Kappler vol. 1.
treaties.json lists Royce 565 and 574 here and again under cession-1874-04-15 (565) and cession-1874-08-19 (574); the same lands appear under three entries.

plain.promised: In 1873 the President set apart one large reservation in northern Montana, down to the Sun River, for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfoot and River Crow. It was an order, not a treaty, and promised no payment.
plain.happened: In 1874 Congress and the President moved the southern line north, taking the land below it. The Court of Claims found in 1935 that 12,261,749.76 acres of the tribes' 1855 treaty land were taken without compensation.
plain.today: The court valued the land at $6,130,874.88, cut by offsets to $622,465.57, paid in 1935 without interest. A later claim for interest was barred. The Blackfeet Nation says each agreement took huge parts of its land.
